text:
Ravi: Running into a snag when mounting my host ~/.redwood into the test container — redwoodctl fails to write profiles.json with EACCES.
Marta: That usually means the UID inside the container doesn't match the host file owner. What does `ls -ln ~/.redwood` show?
Ravi: `drwx------ 3 1001 1001 96 Mar 12 10:02 /home/ravi/.redwood` but the container process is uid 1000.
Jonah: Two immediate workarounds: chown on the host (`sudo chown -R 1000:1000 ~/.redwood`) or run the container with `--user 1001`. Both are meh for CI images.
Ravi: I patched our CI by changing the build step to `chown -R $LOCAL_UID:$LOCAL_GID /home/testuser/.redwood` after apt install. Unblocks tests.
Marta: Suggestion: redwoodctl should detect an unwritable profile directory early and print an actionable message instead of a generic fs error — include the offending uid/gid and a hint for `chown` or running the container with `--user`.
Jonah: Agreed. Also propose `redwoodctl doctor` that checks ~/.redwood ownership/permissions and a `--ci-fix` flag that attempts chown when run as root in container build contexts.
QA: Small security note: don't recommend CI images that bake-in token-bearing profiles. For system-wide installs recommend writing configs to `/etc/redwood` and keeping per-user profiles out of golden images.
ci-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/5342 — "devex: detect unwritable ~/.redwood in container/CI, improve error message, add doctor + --ci-fix" (labels: devex, ci, priority: low)
Marta: I'll add a Docker Compose example to the docs recommending mapping local UID/GID:
```
services:
  app:
    user: "${LOCAL_UID}:${LOCAL_GID}"
    volumes:
      - ~/.redwood:/home/appuser/.redwood
```
Ravi: Thanks — will update our CI and follow the issue for the doctor/auto-fix work.
